sentiment: Something in us keeps rebuilding what it loses; the shape outlives the damage, quietly regrowing toward the form it always was.

stories.title: F-Droid 2.0
stories.summary: A free app store ships its next chapter after years of quiet upkeep. Independence is not declared once and kept — it is regrown every day by people who refuse to let a commons go dark.

stories.title: Why is the liver so weirdly regenerative?
stories.summary: The liver rebuilds most of itself from the part that remains. Loss is not deletion here; the tissue remembers the whole shape and grows patiently back toward it.

stories.title: 2DWillNeverDie
stories.summary: A home for flat, hand-made worlds that outlast the engines built to render them. Old forms survive not because they were replaced, but because someone kept drawing them.
